description: The entity model this SRS prescribes. The legacy system stores everything in ONE physical table of ten columns with no relationships, no foreign keys and no reference tables; the entities below are the logical model the target must realise, derived from the data-domain pass's bounded contexts and the structural pass's column-level evidence. The split of the single legacy row into Student, StudentContactPoint and GuardianReference is a target-state design, not a description of a separable present state.
schema_limitation: CRITICAL AND LOAD-BEARING: the legacy column data types, nullability, declared widths, validation rules, key and index definitions are NOT ESTABLISHED, and two Discovery passes disagree about them — one reports them unknown and refuses to guess, another asserts declared types recovered from binary type bytes (synthesis contradictions CON-001 and CON-002). The attribute types below are therefore the types this SRS PRESCRIBES for the target, chosen to satisfy REQ-037, and they are NOT a transcription of the source schema. NO TARGET DDL MAY BE GENERATED AND NO MIGRATION MAPPING MAY BE WRITTEN until one session against the store through a database engine resolves the source side (synthesis open question OQ-003). Two further source-side facts must be settled in the same session: whether duplicate or empty roll numbers exist, which REQ-039 requires to be resolved before load, and the authoritative row count, which the passes dispute (CON-003).

entities.description: The record subject. Identity and demographic attributes of one student. Corresponds to the data-domain pass's Student aggregate root in the Student Identity and Contact context.

attributes.name: student_id
constraints: enforced unique primary key declared in the schema (REQ-036)
system-generated, never operator-supplied
attributes.traces_to_column: none — PRESCRIBED NEW. The legacy table had no surrogate key and no autonumber column; its key was the business roll number itself, which is a text column admitting the empty string and ordering lexically.

attributes.name: roll_number
attributes.type: string, fixed maximum length, declared format
constraints: enforced unique (REQ-004, REQ-036)
non-empty — the empty string is not an admissible value
immutable once the record exists (REQ-007)
format validated on entry (REQ-003)

attributes.name: first_name
constraints: presence and maximum length validated before persistence (REQ-003)

attributes.name: last_name
constraints: presence and maximum length validated before persistence (REQ-003)

attributes.name: gender_code
constraints: must reference a stored GenderCode (REQ-038)
every value participates in exactly one statistical bucket with a reconciling total (REQ-019)

attributes.name: date_of_birth
constraints: stored and compared as a date value independent of any client display culture (REQ-017)
plausibility validated — not in the future, and consistent with the admission year (REQ-017)

attributes.name: lifecycle_state
constraints: only Active records appear in the standard list, search and statistics (REQ-014)
attributes.traces_to_column: none — PRESCRIBED NEW. The legacy schema had no status column at all, so a record's state was its existence and enrolled, graduated and withdrawn were indistinguishable.

attributes.name: created_by, created_at, modified_by, modified_at, row_version
constraints: written by the system on every mutation, never operator-supplied (REQ-030)
row_version drives optimistic concurrency detection (REQ-032)
attributes.traces_to_column: none — PRESCRIBED NEW. The legacy schema carried no audit, provenance, soft-delete or row-version column, and with no authentication there was no actor to attribute a change to.

relationships.cascade_behavior: contact points follow the student's lifecycle state; removal is the retained audited state change, never a physical cascade delete (REQ-014)

as above. CARDINALITY UNCONFIRMED: modelled as one-to-many so the model does not foreclose a second enrolment, but whether a student may hold more than one is routed as synthesis open question OQ-013. The legacy system could express only one, because course and admission year were columns on the student's own row.

constraints.description: Roll number is unique across all records and cannot be the empty string.
Date of birth must be plausible relative to the admission year.

entities.description: A telephone contact for a student, modelled as its own entity so that a second number is a row rather than a second column, and so that each number can carry its own type and data subject. The legacy system held exactly two mobile-number columns on the student row.

attributes.name: contact_point_id
constraints: primary key

attributes.name: student_id
constraints: foreign key to Student, enforced in the schema
attributes.traces_to_column: none — PRESCRIBED NEW. The legacy database declared no foreign key at all, having only one table.

attributes.name: telephone_number
attributes.type: string, declared maximum length, declared format
constraints: MUST be stored in a type able to represent every value the interface accepts (REQ-037)
format validated for the configured locale (REQ-003)
attributes.evidence: BR-017; synthesis SYN-MCF-003. The legacy columns were reported as a four-byte integer type that cannot hold a ten-digit number at all, while the interface accepted one without complaint — the single clearest reason this attribute must not be typed by copying the source.

attributes.name: is_primary
constraints: exactly one primary contact point per student
attributes.traces_to_column: derived from the legacy column position — MobNo was primary by convention only, never declared

attributes.name: data_subject
constraints: MUST be recorded explicitly, never inferred from column position
attributes.evidence: data-domains.json:open_questions — whose telephone number the alternate number is was raised as an open question and is unresolved; routed as synthesis open question OQ-009. Recording the subject explicitly is what makes an erasure request answerable.

constraints.description: A telephone number must be storable in full; no value the interface accepts may overflow or be truncated.

entities.description: Personal data about a named third party held in relation to a student. Modelled as a separate entity because it concerns a DIFFERENT DATA SUBJECT from the record subject, which the legacy single-row design made impossible to express.

attributes.name: guardian_reference_id
constraints: primary key

attributes.name: student_id
constraints: foreign key to Student

attributes.name: guardian_name
constraints: presence and maximum length validated when supplied (REQ-003)

attributes.name: relationship_to_student
attributes.type: string or reference to a stored relationship type
attributes.traces_to_column: none — PRESCRIBED NEW. The legacy column name presumed the relationship rather than recording it.

constraints.description: Guardian data is personal data about a second, unconsented data subject and MUST be separately identifiable so that a retention or erasure obligation can be applied to it independently of the student record.

entities.description: A student's enrolment on a course in an intake year. The data-domain pass's Student Enrolment context, and the weakest boundary in that pass's own assessment — it concedes this is its lowest-confidence arbitration. The legacy system expressed it as two columns on the student's own row, so only one enrolment per student could exist.

attributes.name: enrolment_id
constraints: primary key

attributes.name: student_id
constraints: foreign key to Student

attributes.name: course_code
constraints: must reference a stored CourseCode (REQ-038)

attributes.name: intake_year
constraints: compared and sorted arithmetically, never as text (REQ-021)
must reference a stored intake year with no code change required for a new one (REQ-038)
attributes.evidence: BR-015; BR-074. The legacy column stored the year as text and the interface offered a static list that expired at 2023, so no later intake could be recorded at all.

relationships.cascade_behavior: restrict — a course in use may not be removed from the reference data

constraints.description: Intake year must be stored and compared as a number so that ordering and range queries are arithmetic.

entities.description: Reference data: the courses a student may enrol on. PRESCRIBED NEW AS STORED DATA. In the legacy system this set had no system of record at all — it was restated as literals in at least eight places across two interface definition files and the statistics queries, so adding a course required a code change in every one of them.

attributes.name: course_code
constraints: primary key
attributes.traces_to_column: none — the legacy values were interface literals, not stored data

attributes.name: course_name
constraints: human-readable; used for operator-visible labels (NFR-003)

attributes.name: is_active
constraints: an inactive course remains referencable by historical enrolments but is not offered for new ones
a course with no enrolments is still reported, as zero (REQ-020)

constraints.description: The reference set has exactly one system of record and is not restated in interface or query code.

entities.description: Reference data: the gender values a student record may carry. PRESCRIBED NEW AS STORED DATA. The legacy set was enforced in two interface files and nowhere in the database, and critically the statistics counted only two of its three values with no reconciling total, so a record holding the third was storable and invisible in every statistic.

attributes.name: gender_code
constraints: primary key
attributes.traces_to_column: none — the legacy values were interface literals

attributes.name: gender_label
constraints: human-readable

attributes.name: include_in_statistics
constraints: EVERY value, including any excluded one, participates in exactly one bucket of the reported breakdown, and the breakdown reconciles to the total record count (REQ-019)

constraints.description: The statistical breakdown over this reference set must sum to the total record count, with an explicit residual bucket for absent, empty or out-of-set values.

entities.description: Reference data: the academic intake years a student may be admitted in. PRESCRIBED NEW AS STORED DATA, and the single clearest case for doing so: the legacy set was a static interface list of 2019 to 2023 duplicated across four locations, so no intake after 2023 could be recorded at all, and the statistics derived their cohort buckets by subtraction from a separate hardcoded constant.

attributes.name: intake_year
constraints: primary key
arithmetic comparison and ordering (REQ-021)
attributes.traces_to_column: none — the legacy values were interface literals

attributes.name: is_open_for_admission
constraints: a new intake year becomes selectable by adding a row, with no code change (REQ-038)

constraints.description: Academic-year statistics are derived from the current date at computation time and from this stored set, never from a compiled-in year constant.
